CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right finger pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sharon Brooks is a 48-year-old female presenting with right index finger pain. Injury occurred Sunday during skiing when she was attempting moguls and her ski strap became caught on her finger, causing it to bend backward. Pain is persistent and worsened by movement. Patient has attempted ice and ibuprofen for management without adequate relief.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Constipation, recent. Appendectomy at age 18.

MEDICATIONS
Miralax for constipation. Ibuprofen for current pain.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recreational skiing.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Tenderness over distal phalanx and distal interphalangeal joint. No tenderness over proximal interphalangeal joint or metacarpophalangeal joint. Pain with flexion. Able to bend and extend finger. Able to touch thumb with affected finger.

RESULTS
X-rays of right hand show no fractures with normal alignment.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right hand index finger contusion on tip of finger. Aluminum foam splint recommended. Motrin 600 mg every 6 hours for approximately one week. Patient instructed to call and return if symptoms do not improve.
